title: Matthabanks (Great South Beach)
summary: Matthabanks is a placename for the Great South Beach opposite Brookhaven, on the barrier island now generally known as Fire Island.
history_content: The placename belongs to the south-shore barrier beach landscape tied to Unkechaug and Brookhaven land history. The beach bounds connect Matthabanks with Owenamchock to the east and Nanmicake to the west.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted through related Algonquian forms as referring to a riverbank, brim, edge, or sitting place. The interpretation emphasizes an edge-place, fitting a barrier beach or bank landscape.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place naming is a powerful catalyst for reconciliation, provoking a deeper awareness of a location’s history and culture.”

— Clean State, A transformative, state-wide Aboriginal Place Naming Project (2025), Opening statement

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
whereintheworld_content: Map location note: the pin is placed on the Fire Island barrier beach south of Brookhaven/Bellport to represent the Great South Beach association; it is not an exact historic boundary point.
